To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maternal obesity and glucose intolerance are common in Mexican-American women and may be associated with increased birthweight, and that the prevalence of obesity and glucose tolerance in this population may be increasing.

(i) the prevalence of obesity and glucose tolerance during pregnancy is high among Mexican-Americans; and (ii) the adequacy of the low birthweight rate as a measure of fetal health and risk may be obscured because of the prevalence of obesity in Mexican-American women.

obesity and glucose intolerance are common among Mexican-Americans and that these conditions are associated with fetal and child health risks that may be masked by the high birthweights and low prevalence of low birthweight in the community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of obesity, impaired glucose tolerance, diabetes and other metabolic abnormalities on birthweight, and the subsequent health status of Mexican-American women and children.
the impact of obesity, glucose intolerance and diabetes during pregnancy on birthweight in Mexican-American infants and the subsequent health of mothers and their offspring.
the impact of obesity, impaired glucose tolerance, diabetes and other metabolic disorders during pregnancy on maternal and neonatal risk in the Mexican-American population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the health status of Mexican-American women and children is a complex and dynamic process.
the health of the Mexican American population is not as good as the health of the general U.S. population, but that it is better than the health of other ethnic minority groups.

maternal obesity and glucose intolerance in pregnancy are common among Mexican-Americans and are associated with increased risk of fetal overgrowth and subsequent obesity and type-2 diabetes in mother, child and adolescent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

obesity and glucose intolerance are common during pregnancy among Mexican-American women, and may be contributing to the high rates of obesity and type II diabetes in Mexican-American infants and young adults.
the prevalence of maternal obesity and glucose intolerance is high among Mexican-American women, and that these conditions have not received adequate public health attention.

the high prevalence of obesity and glucose tolerance among Mexican-American women during pregnancy may mask the impact of these conditions on fetal overgrowth and on subsequent obesity and type-2 diabetes in mother, child and adolescent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is a serious problem among pregnant women, and that this is especially true for Mexican-American women.
the prevalence of obesity, impaired glucose tolerance, gestational diabetes, and type 2 DM are high among Mexican-American women.

we need to do more to address the problem of obesity among women of reproductive age and during pregnancy, and that we need to pay closer attention to the health status of infants of obese women, especially those with impaired glucose tolerance and/or diabetes during pregnancy.
